questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following quantities have the dimensions of velocity?
questions.explanation: Displacement/time, acceleration × time, and force/mass all have dimensions LT⁻¹. Work/time has dimensions of power.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 5 s. What is its final speed?
questions.explanation: Using v = u + at = 0 + 2 × 5 = 10 m/s.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A vector of magnitude 10 units makes an angle of 30° with the positive x-axis. What are its x- and y-components?
questions.explanation: Aₓ = A cos 30° = 5√3 and Aᵧ = A sin 30° = 5.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A net force of 12 N acts on a 3 kg object. What is the object's acceleration?
questions.explanation: From F = ma, a = 12/3 = 4 m/s².
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A constant force of 10 N moves an object 3 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which statements about uniform circular motion are correct?

options.text: The acceleration points toward the centre
The direction of velocity continually changes

questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, speed is constant but velocity changes direction; centripetal acceleration points inward.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the distance between two point masses is doubled, while the masses remain unchanged, the gravitational force becomes:
questions.explanation: Newton's law gives F ∝ 1/r², so doubling r reduces force to one-fourth.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Within the limit of proportionality, which relationship describes Hooke's law?

options.text: Stress is proportional to strain squared

questions.explanation: For a linearly elastic material within the proportional limit, stress ∝ strain.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: How much heat is needed to raise the temperature of 2 kg of a substance with specific heat capacity 500 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ by 4 K?
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 2 m. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Wave speed v = fλ = 50 × 2 = 100 m/s.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two point charges exert a force F on each other in vacuum. If one charge is doubled and their separation is also doubled, the new force is:
questions.explanation: F ∝ q₁q₂/r². Doubling one charge gives ×2 and doubling distance gives ÷4, so the new force is F/2.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 6 Ω resistor is connected across a 12 V ideal battery. What current flows through it?
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which factors affect the magnitude of magnetic force on a moving charge in a uniform magnetic field?

options.text: Angle between velocity and magnetic field

questions.explanation: F = |q|vB sin θ, so all four factors can affect the magnitude.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Faraday's law, the magnitude of induced emf in a coil depends on the rate of change of:
questions.explanation: The induced emf magnitude is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a sinusoidal alternating voltage with peak value 100 V, the RMS voltage is approximately:
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Light travels from air into glass. Which statements are correct for a ray incident obliquely on the glass surface?

options.text: It bends toward the normal if glass has a higher refractive index

questions.explanation: Frequency remains constant at a boundary. In glass, light speed and wavelength decrease; the ray bends toward the normal when entering a higher-index medium.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the frequency of incident light above the threshold frequency increases the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons. Which relation expresses this?
questions.explanation: Einstein's photoelectric equation is Kmax = hf − ϕ, where ϕ is the work function.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two forces of magnitudes $6\text{ N}$ and $8\text{ N}$ act at right angles to each other. What is the magnitude of their resultant force?
questions.explanation: For two orthogonal vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$, the resultant magnitude is $R = \sqrt{A^2 + B^2} = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = \sqrt{100} = 10\text{ N}$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A projectile is launched from ground level at an angle $\theta = 30^\circ$ with an initial velocity $u = 40\text{ m/s}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, what is the maximum height attained?
questions.explanation: Maximum height of a projectile is given by $H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} = \frac{40^2 \times (\sin 30^\circ)^2}{2 \times 10} = \frac{1600 \times (0.5)^2}{20} = \frac{1600 \times 0.25}{20} = 20\text{ m}$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the linear momentum of an object is doubled while keeping its mass constant, its kinetic energy increases by:
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy $K = \frac{p^2}{2m}$. If $p$ is doubled ($p' = 2p$), $K' = \frac{(2p)^2}{2m} = 4K$. Percentage increase is $\frac{K' - K}{K} \times 100\% = \frac{4K - K}{K} \times 100\% = 300\%$.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: At what altitude above the surface of the Earth will the acceleration due to gravity become $\frac{g}{4}$, where $R$ is the Earth's radius?
questions.explanation: At altitude $h$, $g' = g \left(\frac{R}{R+h}\right)^2$. Setting $g' = \frac{g}{4}$ gives $\left(\frac{R}{R+h}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4} \implies \frac{R}{R+h} = \frac{1}{2} \implies R+h = 2R \implies h = R$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A wire of Young's modulus $Y$ and cross-sectional area $A$ is stretched by a force $F$ producing elongation $\Delta L$. The elastic potential energy stored per unit volume in the wire is:
questions.explanation: The energy density (energy stored per unit volume) in a stretched elastic wire is $u = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Stress} \times \text{Strain} = \frac{1}{2} Y (\text{Strain})^2 = \frac{\text{Stress}^2}{2Y}$.
questions.curriculum_note: Conceptual Practice; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: At what temperature do the Celsius and Fahrenheit temperature scales indicate the exact same numerical value?
questions.explanation: Using $\frac{C}{5} = \frac{F - 32}{9}$ and setting $C = F = x$: $\frac{x}{5} = \frac{x - 32}{9} \implies 9x = 5x - 160 \implies 4x = -160 \implies x = -40$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: During an adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas, the thermodynamic work done by the gas is done entirely at the expense of its:
questions.explanation: By the first law of thermodynamics, $dQ = dU + dW$. In an adiabatic process, $dQ = 0$, so $dW = -dU$. Therefore, work is accomplished strictly by reducing internal energy.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A convex lens of focal length $20\text{ cm}$ is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length $30\text{ cm}$. What is the effective power of the combination?
questions.explanation: Power $P_1 = \frac{1}{0.20} = +5\text{ D}$, $P_2 = -\frac{1}{0.30} = -3.33\text{ D}$. Total power $P = P_1 + P_2 = 5 - 3.33 = +1.67\text{ D}$. The combination acts as a convergent lens.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A solid sphere and a hollow cylinder of equal mass $M$ and radius $R$ roll down an inclined plane without slipping. Which reaches the bottom first?

options.text: Depends on the angle of inclination

questions.explanation: Acceleration along incline is $a = \frac{g \sin\theta}{1 + I/(MR^2)}$. For solid sphere, $I = \frac{2}{5}MR^2 \implies k^2/R^2 = 0.4$. For hollow cylinder, $I = MR^2 \implies k^2/R^2 = 1.0$. Smaller moment of inertia ratio produces higher linear acceleration.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM), when the displacement of the particle is half of its amplitude ($y = A/2$), the ratio of its kinetic energy to potential energy is:
questions.explanation: $U = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 y^2 = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 (A/2)^2 = \frac{1}{8}m\omega^2 A^2$. Total energy $E = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 A^2$. Thus $K = E - U = \frac{3}{8}m\omega^2 A^2$. The ratio $K/U = 3/1$.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A potentiometer wire of length $10\text{ m}$ has a resistance of $20\text{ }\Omega$. It is connected in series with a battery of EMF $2.5\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $5\text{ }\Omega$. What is the potential gradient along the wire?
questions.explanation: Current $I = \frac{E}{R + r} = \frac{2.5}{20 + 5} = \frac{2.5}{25} = 0.1\text{ A}$. Potential drop across the $10\text{ m}$ wire is $V = I \times R = 0.1 \times 20 = 2.0\text{ V}$. Potential gradient $k = \frac{V}{L} = \frac{2.0\text{ V}}{10\text{ m}} = 0.2\text{ V/m}$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Motion of charged particles in magnetic fields
questions.question: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly with velocity $v$. The kinetic energy of the charged particle in the magnetic field:
questions.explanation: The magnetic Lorentz force $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v} \times \vec{B})$ is always perpendicular to the velocity vector $\vec{v}$. Since $\vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = 0$, no mechanical work is done by the magnetic field, and the kinetic energy remains invariant.
questions.curriculum_note: Conceptual Practice; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When the current in an inductor of self-inductance $L = 2\text{ H}$ decreases from $5\text{ A}$ to $1\text{ A}$ in $0.1\text{ s}$, the magnitude of the induced EMF is:
questions.explanation: By Faraday-Lenz law of electromagnetic induction, $|e| = L \left|\frac{di}{dt}\right| = 2 \times \frac{|1 - 5|}{0.1} = 2 \times \frac{4}{0.1} = 80\text{ V}$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the de Broglie wavelength associated with an electron accelerated through a potential difference of $100\text{ V}$?
questions.explanation: For an electron accelerated through potential difference $V$, $\lambda = \frac{1.227}{\sqrt{V}}\text{ nm} = \frac{1.227}{\sqrt{100}}\text{ nm} = \frac{1.227}{10}\text{ nm} = 0.1227\text{ nm} \approx 0.123\text{ nm}$.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is $15\text{ days}$. What fraction of the original sample remains undecayed after $45\text{ days}$?
questions.explanation: Number of half-lives elapsed $n = \frac{t}{T_{1/2}} = \frac{45}{15} = 3$. Remaining fraction is $\frac{N}{N_0} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{8}$.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an intrinsic semiconductor at room temperature, when an acceptor trivalent impurity (such as Boron or Indium) is doped into pure Silicon, it creates:

options.text: An n-type semiconductor where electrons are majority carriers
A p-type semiconductor where holes are majority carriers
An intrinsic dielectric with zero conductance

questions.explanation: Trivalent atoms have 3 valence electrons. When sharing bonds with tetravalent Silicon, a deficiency of one electron creates a hole. Doping trivalent atoms therefore forms a p-type semiconductor with holes as majority carriers.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental physical quantity?
questions.explanation: Fundamental physical quantities are the basic building blocks of measurement in physics. Length is a fundamental quantity, while force, energy, and velocity are derived from fundamental quantities.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the SI unit of mass?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of mass is the kilogram (kg). It is the standard unit used in scientific measurements, while gram, pound, and ounce are not standard SI units.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What are the dimensions of energy in terms of fundamental quantities?
questions.explanation: Energy is defined as the capacity to do work. Its dimensions are derived from the work equation (W = F × d), which leads to [M^1 L^2 T^-2], where M is mass, L is length, and T is time.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes systematic error?

options.text: Errors that occur due to unknown fluctuations in measurement.
Errors that consistently occur in the same direction.
Errors that can be reduced by averaging multiple measurements.
Errors due to limitations in measuring equipment.

questions.explanation: Systematic errors are consistent and repeatable inaccuracies that occur in the same direction, often due to a flaw in the measurement system or technique. They can skew results in a consistent manner.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When rounding the number 0.00456 to two significant figures, what is the correct result?
questions.explanation: To round 0.00456 to two significant figures, we look at the first two non-zero digits (4 and 5). The next digit (6) rounds the second digit up to 6, resulting in 0.0046.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A wheel rotates with a constant angular acceleration of 2 rad/s². If its initial angular velocity is 5 rad/s, what is its angular velocity after 3 seconds?
questions.explanation: Using the formula for angular velocity under constant acceleration, ω = ω₀ + αt, where ω₀ is the initial angular velocity (5 rad/s), α is angular acceleration (2 rad/s²), and t is time (3 s), we find ω = 5 + (2 × 3) = 11 rad/s.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A force of 10 N is applied perpendicular to a lever arm of length 2 m. What is the torque produced by this force?
questions.explanation: Torque (τ) is calculated using the formula τ = r × F, where r is the distance from the pivot (2 m) and F is the force applied (10 N). Thus, τ = 2 m × 10 N = 20 Nm.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following has the greatest moment of inertia about an axis through its center of mass?
questions.explanation: The moment of inertia depends on the mass distribution. A hollow sphere has a greater moment of inertia compared to a solid sphere or solid cylinder due to its mass being further from the axis of rotation.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A figure skater spins with arms extended and then pulls her arms in. What happens to her angular velocity as she does this?
questions.explanation: According to the conservation of angular momentum, when the skater pulls her arms in, her moment of inertia decreases, leading to an increase in angular velocity to conserve angular momentum.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the formula for rotational kinetic energy of a rotating object?
questions.explanation: The formula for rotational kinetic energy (KE) is KE = 1/2 I ω², where I is the moment of inertia and ω is the angular velocity. This is analogous to translational kinetic energy.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector quantity because it has both magnitude and direction. In contrast, temperature, mass, and time are scalar quantities as they only possess magnitude.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the graphical representation of a vector called?
questions.explanation: Vectors are graphically represented by arrows, where the length of the arrow indicates the magnitude and the direction of the arrow indicates the direction of the vector.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If vector A has a magnitude of 5 units and vector B has a magnitude of 3 units, what is the maximum possible magnitude of the resultant vector when they are added?
questions.explanation: The maximum magnitude of the resultant vector occurs when both vectors are in the same direction, which means you simply add their magnitudes: 5 + 3 = 8 units.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding the resolution of vectors?

options.text: Any vector can be resolved into two perpendicular components.
Vectors can only be resolved into parallel components.
Only scalar quantities can be resolved.
Resolution is only applicable to 2D vectors.

questions.explanation: It is a fundamental principle in physics that any vector can be resolved into two perpendicular components, typically along the x and y axes, allowing for easier analysis of vector interactions.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the result of the vector product of two parallel vectors?
questions.explanation: The vector product (cross product) of two parallel vectors is zero because the sine of the angle between them (which is 0 degrees) equals zero, resulting in a zero vector.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following best defines periodic motion?

options.text: Motion that repeats at regular intervals.
Motion that occurs in a straight line.
Motion that occurs without a specific pattern.

questions.explanation: Periodic motion is defined as motion that repeats itself at regular intervals, such as the swinging of a pendulum or the oscillation of a spring. This characteristic of repeating cycles is key to identifying periodic motion.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In simple harmonic motion (SHM), the acceleration of an object is:

options.text: Directly proportional to its displacement from the equilibrium position.

questions.explanation: In SHM, the acceleration is directly proportional to the negative of the displacement from the equilibrium position, according to Hooke's Law. This means that as the object moves further from equilibrium, the restoring force and hence the acceleration increases.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the frequency of a simple harmonic oscillator is doubled, what happens to its period?
questions.explanation: The period of a simple harmonic oscillator is the reciprocal of the frequency. If the frequency is doubled, the period is halved, as given by the formula T = 1/f, where T is the period and f is the frequency.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a simple harmonic oscillator, which form of energy is maximum at the maximum displacement?
questions.explanation: At maximum displacement in simple harmonic motion, the object momentarily comes to rest, thus all of its energy is potential energy. The kinetic energy is zero at this point, while total mechanical energy remains constant.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What effect do damping forces have on oscillations in a damped harmonic oscillator?

options.text: They increase the amplitude over time.
They cause the amplitude to decrease over time.
They have no effect on the frequency of oscillation.
They convert kinetic energy into thermal energy only.

questions.explanation: Damping forces, such as friction, act opposite to the direction of motion, causing the amplitude of oscillations to decrease over time. This results in energy loss to the environment, affecting the oscillator's behavior.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object is said to be in motion when it changes its position with respect to a reference point. Which of the following scenarios illustrates this concept?

options.text: A car parked on the side of the road.
A person walking towards a bus stop.
A clock showing the same time.

questions.explanation: An object is in motion if it changes its position over time relative to a fixed point. In this case, the person walking towards the bus stop is changing their position, thus demonstrating motion.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the difference between speed and velocity?

options.text: Speed is a scalar quantity, while velocity is a vector quantity.
Speed can be negative, but velocity cannot.
Speed includes direction, but velocity does not.
Speed is always constant, while velocity varies.

questions.explanation: Speed is defined as the distance traveled per unit of time and is a scalar quantity, while velocity includes both speed and direction, making it a vector quantity.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s². What is the velocity of the object after 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: Using the equation of motion v = u + at, where u = 0 m/s (starting from rest), a = 2 m/s², and t = 5 s, we find v = 0 + (2)(5) = 10 m/s.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ball is thrown horizontally from a height of 20 meters. Ignoring air resistance, how long does it take to hit the ground?
questions.explanation: Using the formula for free fall, t = √(2h/g), where h = 20 m and g = 9.81 m/s², we find t ≈ √(20/4.905) ≈ 2 seconds.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a velocity-time graph, a straight line parallel to the time axis indicates which of the following?
questions.explanation: A straight line parallel to the time axis in a velocity-time graph indicates that the velocity remains constant over time, thus there is no acceleration.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes a fluid?

options.text: A fluid is a substance that can flow and does not have a definite shape.
A fluid is a solid that can change its shape under stress.
Fluids can only be liquids and not gases.
A fluid is any substance that has a fixed volume.

questions.explanation: A fluid is defined as a substance that can flow and conforms to the shape of its container. This includes both liquids and gases, making option A the correct statement.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure is defined as force per unit area. The SI unit of pressure is the Pascal (Pa), which is equal to one Newton per square meter.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Pascal's law, when pressure is applied to a confined fluid, it is transmitted:

options.text: Only to the surface of the fluid.
Only to the bottom of the container.

questions.explanation: Pascal's law states that pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions throughout the fluid. Therefore, option C is correct.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Archimedes' principle, when an object is submerged in a fluid, it experiences an upward buoyant force equal to:

options.text: The weight of the fluid displaced by the object.
The weight of the object itself.

questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle states that the buoyant force acting on a submerged object is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object, making option A correct.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is a consequence of Bernoulli's principle?

options.text: As the speed of a fluid increases, its pressure decreases.
Fluids at rest exert pressure equally in all directions.
The total energy of a fluid remains constant.
All of the above are true.

questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle states that an increase in the speed of a fluid occurs simultaneously with a decrease in pressure. Therefore, option A is the correct consequence of Bernoulli's principle.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes inertia?

options.text: It is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion.
It is the force required to change an object's motion.
It is the acceleration of an object in motion.
It is the mass of an object multiplied by its velocity.

questions.explanation: Inertia is defined as the property of matter that causes it to resist any change in its state of motion, including changes to its speed or direction. According to Newton's first law, an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If a force of 10 N is applied to an object of mass 2 kg, what will be its acceleration?
questions.explanation: According to Newton's second law of motion, acceleration (a) can be calculated using the formula F = ma, where F is the force and m is the mass. Here, a = F/m = 10 N / 2 kg = 5 m/s².
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 3 kg object moving at 4 m/s collides with a stationary 2 kg object. Assuming an elastic collision, what is the velocity of the 2 kg object after the collision?
questions.explanation: In an elastic collision, momentum is conserved. The total momentum before the collision equals the total momentum after the collision. Using the formula for conservation of momentum, we find that the 2 kg object moves at 2.4 m/s after the collision.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following factors does NOT affect the force of friction between two surfaces?

options.text: The nature of the surfaces in contact.

questions.explanation: The force of friction is influenced by the nature of the surfaces, the normal force (weight of the object), and surface roughness. However, the area of contact does not significantly affect the force of friction because frictional force is proportional to the normal force and the coefficient of friction.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the centripetal force acting on a 5 kg object moving in a circular path of radius 3 m with a speed of 6 m/s?
questions.explanation: Centripetal force (Fc) can be calculated using the formula Fc = mv²/r. Substituting the values, we get Fc = (5 kg)(6 m/s)² / (3 m) = 12 N.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following best describes an open thermodynamic system?

options.text: A system that can exchange both energy and matter with its surroundings.
A system that can exchange only energy but not matter.
A system that can exchange only matter but not energy.
A system that does not exchange either energy or matter.

questions.explanation: An open thermodynamic system allows for the transfer of both energy and matter, making it distinct from closed or isolated systems. This definition aligns with standard thermodynamic principles.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the relationship expressed by the first law of thermodynamics?
questions.explanation: The first law of thermodynamics states that the change in internal energy (ΔU) of a system is equal to the heat added to the system (Q) plus the work done on the system (W). This formula is fundamental in thermodynamics.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In the context of thermal equilibrium, which statement is accurate?

options.text: Heat flows from a cooler body to a hotter body.
Heat flows from a hotter body to a cooler body.
No heat transfer occurs between bodies at different temperatures.
Thermal equilibrium is reached when bodies are at different temperatures.

questions.explanation: Thermal equilibrium occurs when two bodies are at the same temperature, leading to no net heat flow. Heat naturally flows from a hotter to a cooler body until equilibrium is established.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: During an adiabatic process, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: No heat is exchanged with the surroundings.
The pressure of the gas does not change.
Work done on the gas is equal to heat absorbed.

questions.explanation: An adiabatic process is characterized by the absence of heat exchange with the surroundings (Q = 0). This leads to changes in internal energy being solely due to work done on or by the system.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When a gas expands isothermally, the work done by the gas is given by which of the following expressions?
questions.explanation: For an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, the work done by the gas is calculated using the formula W = nRT ln(Vf/Vi), where n is the number of moles, R is the ideal gas constant, and Vf and Vi are the final and initial volumes, respectively.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Work done by a constant force
questions.question: A constant force of 5 N is applied to move an object 3 meters in the direction of the force. How much work is done by the force?
questions.explanation: Work done is calculated using the formula W = F × d × cos(θ). Here, F = 5 N, d = 3 m, and θ = 0° (force and displacement are in the same direction). Thus, W = 5 N × 3 m × cos(0°) = 15 J.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Work done by a variable force
questions.question: If the work done by a variable force on an object varies with distance as W = 2x^2, what is the work done when the object moves from x=1 m to x=3 m?
questions.explanation: The work done is calculated by integrating the force over distance. W = ∫(2x^2)dx from 1 to 3, which results in [2/3 * x^3] from 1 to 3 = (2/3 * 27) - (2/3 * 1) = 18 - (2/3) = 16 J.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object of mass 4 kg is moving with a speed of 3 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy (KE) is given by the formula KE = 1/2 mv^2. Substituting the values, KE = 1/2 * 4 kg * (3 m/s)^2 = 1/2 * 4 * 9 = 18 J.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the potential energy of a 10 kg mass held at a height of 5 m above the ground? (Assume g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Potential energy (PE) is calculated using the formula PE = mgh. Here, m = 10 kg, g = 9.8 m/s², and h = 5 m. Thus, PE = 10 * 9.8 * 5 = 490 J.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a closed system, if the potential energy of an object decreases by 100 J, what happens to its kinetic energy assuming mechanical energy is conserved?
questions.explanation: According to the conservation of mechanical energy, if potential energy decreases, kinetic energy must increase by the same amount to keep the total mechanical energy constant. Therefore, if potential energy decreases by 100 J, kinetic energy increases by 100 J.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statements illustrates a limitation of the first law of thermodynamics?

options.text: Energy can be created and destroyed.
Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body.
The total energy of an isolated system remains constant.
Work done by a system is equal to the change in internal energy.

questions.explanation: The first law of thermodynamics states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed. However, it does not account for the directionality of heat flow, which is governed by the second law. The second law indicates that heat naturally flows from hot to cold, not the reverse without external work.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a heat engine?

options.text: To convert thermal energy into mechanical work.
To transfer heat from a cold reservoir to a hot reservoir.
To increase the temperature of a working fluid.
To reduce the entropy of a system.

questions.explanation: The fundamental purpose of a heat engine is to convert thermal energy obtained from a heat source into mechanical work. This process involves absorbing heat from a high-temperature reservoir and performing work as it releases some heat to a lower temperature reservoir.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Carnot's theorem, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: No real engine can be more efficient than a Carnot engine.
Carnot engines can operate without any heat loss.
The efficiency of all engines is the same regardless of their design.
Carnot engines are only applicable to reversible processes.

questions.explanation: Carnot's theorem establishes that no heat engine operating between two heat reservoirs can be more efficient than a Carnot engine operating between the same reservoirs. This sets a fundamental limit on the efficiency of heat engines.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What does the concept of entropy in thermodynamics primarily represent?

options.text: The total energy of a system.
The degree of disorder or randomness in a system.
The heat content of a system.
The work output of a thermodynamic process.

questions.explanation: Entropy is a measure of the degree of disorder or randomness in a system. It quantifies the energy in a system that is not available to do work, thus playing a key role in the second law of thermodynamics which states that the total entropy of an isolated system can never decrease over time.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The coefficient of performance (COP) of a refrigerator is defined as the ratio of which two quantities?

options.text: Heat removed from the cold reservoir to work input.
Work input to heat removed from the hot reservoir.

questions.explanation: The coefficient of performance (COP) of a refrigerator is defined as the ratio of the heat removed from the cold reservoir (Q_C) to the work input (W) required to operate the refrigerator. Thus, COP = Q_C / W, indicating the efficiency of the refrigeration cycle.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object moves in a circular path of radius 2 m and completes one full revolution. What is the angular displacement in radians?
questions.explanation: The angular displacement for one full revolution is equal to 2π radians. Since 2π is approximately 6.28, the correct answer is 6.28 radians.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If an object completes a circular motion with a period of 4 seconds, what is its angular velocity?
questions.explanation: Angular velocity (ω) can be calculated using the formula ω = 2π/T. Substituting T = 4 seconds gives ω = 2π/4 = π/2 ≈ 1.57 rad/s.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object moves in a circle of radius 5 m with a speed of 10 m/s. What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration (a_c) is given by the formula a_c = v²/r. Here, v = 10 m/s and r = 5 m, so a_c = 10²/5 = 100/5 = 20 m/s².
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If a 2 kg object is moving in a circular path of radius 3 m with a speed of 6 m/s, what is the centripetal force acting on it?
questions.explanation: Centripetal force (F_c) can be calculated using the formula F_c = mv²/r. Here, m = 2 kg, v = 6 m/s, and r = 3 m, so F_c = 2 * 6² / 3 = 12 N.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In uniform circular motion, which of the following quantities remains constant?
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the angular velocity remains constant as the object covers equal angles in equal intervals of time, while tangential speed and centripetal acceleration can vary depending on the radius.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What condition must be satisfied for standing waves to form in a string fixed at both ends?

options.text: The length of the string must be an integer multiple of half the wavelength.
The tension in the string must be zero.
The frequency of the wave must be constant.
The amplitude of the wave must be increasing.

questions.explanation: For standing waves to form in a string fixed at both ends, the length of the string must be an integer multiple of half the wavelength, ensuring constructive interference at fixed points (nodes). This condition allows the formation of stable standing wave patterns.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following is the second harmonic frequency of a string with a fundamental frequency of 200 Hz?
questions.explanation: The second harmonic frequency is double the fundamental frequency. Therefore, if the fundamental frequency is 200 Hz, the second harmonic frequency is 2 × 200 Hz = 400 Hz.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an open pipe, where are the nodes and antinodes located for the fundamental frequency?

options.text: Nodes at both ends, antinodes in the middle.
Antinodes at both ends, nodes in the middle.
Nodes at one end and antinodes at the other.
Antinodes at both ends, no nodes.

questions.explanation: In an open pipe, the fundamental frequency has antinodes at both ends and a node in the middle. This is due to the requirement for maximum displacement (antinodes) at the open ends where the air can move freely.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the effect of resonance in an air column when a tuning fork is struck?
questions.explanation: When a tuning fork is struck near an air column that resonates at its frequency, the amplitude of the sound produced increases due to resonance, resulting in louder sound. This occurs because the energy from the fork is effectively transferred to the air column.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is end correction in the context of vibrating pipes?

options.text: The additional length of the pipe required to account for the displacement of the air at the open ends.
The loss of energy due to friction in the pipe.
The change in frequency due to temperature variation.
The adjustment of tension in the pipe.

questions.explanation: End correction is the additional length added to the theoretical length of a vibrating pipe to account for the displacement of air at the open ends. It helps to accurately determine the effective wavelength and frequency of the sound produced in the pipe.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of force is the newton (N). One newton is the force required to accelerate a mass of one kilogram at one metre per second squared.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector quantity because it has both magnitude and direction. Speed, distance, and mass are scalar quantities.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the acceleration of an object moving with constant velocity?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. If velocity remains constant in both magnitude and direction, acceleration is zero.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which equation relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and time for constant acceleration?
questions.explanation: For constant acceleration, final velocity v equals initial velocity u plus acceleration a multiplied by time t.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Newton's second law, the net force acting on an object equals:
questions.explanation: Newton's second law states that the net force on an object equals its mass multiplied by its acceleration.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body remains at rest or continues in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by a net external force. This statement represents:
questions.explanation: Newton's first law is also known as the law of inertia. It describes how an object's motion changes only when a net external force acts on it.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the SI unit of work?
questions.explanation: Work is measured in joules (J). One joule is equal to one newton-metre.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which expression gives the kinetic energy of an object of mass m moving at speed v?
questions.explanation: The kinetic energy of a body moving at speed v is one-half its mass multiplied by the square of its speed.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the approximate acceleration due to gravity near Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: The approximate standard value of gravitational acceleration near Earth's surface is 9.8 m/s².
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Newton's law of universal gravitation, the force between two point masses is inversely proportional to:

options.text: The square of the distance between them

questions.explanation: The gravitational force follows an inverse-square relationship with separation distance: doubling the distance reduces the force to one-quarter, with masses unchanged.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body moves in a circle of radius r with speed v. What is its centripetal acceleration?
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration has magnitude v²/r and is directed toward the centre of the circular path.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Within the elastic limit, Hooke's law states that stress is directly proportional to:
questions.explanation: Within the proportional limit, stress is directly proportional to strain. The ratio of stress to strain is the modulus of elasticity.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The pressure at a depth h in a stationary liquid of density ρ is given by which expression for gauge pressure?
questions.explanation: The gauge pressure in a stationary liquid is P = ρgh, where ρ is density, g is gravitational acceleration, and h is depth.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Why do small liquid droplets tend to have a spherical shape?

options.text: Because surface tension tends to minimize surface area
Because liquids have no intermolecular forces
Because liquid pressure is always zero

questions.explanation: For a given volume, a sphere has the minimum surface area. Surface tension therefore favours a spherical shape for small droplets when other effects are negligible.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the approximate temperature corresponding to 27°C on the Kelvin scale?
questions.explanation: Temperature in kelvin is approximately Celsius temperature plus 273. Thus, 27°C is approximately 300 K.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: How much heat is required to raise the temperature of 2 kg of a substance with specific heat capacity 500 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ by 4 K?
questions.explanation: Using Q = mcΔT, Q = 2 × 500 × 4 = 4000 J.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What happens to the temperature of a pure substance during melting at constant pressure?

options.text: It remains constant until melting is complete

questions.explanation: During melting, supplied heat is used as latent heat to change the phase rather than increase the temperature, assuming equilibrium at constant pressure.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which process takes place at constant pressure?
questions.explanation: An isobaric process occurs at constant pressure.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 4 m. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Wave speed v = fλ = 50 × 4 = 200 m/s.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Sound cannot travel through:
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and requires a material medium to propagate. A vacuum contains no medium to transmit sound.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Constructive interference occurs when two coherent waves meet in phase. What is their phase difference?

options.text: An arbitrary phase difference in every case

questions.explanation: Constructive interference occurs when the phase difference is 2nπ, where n is an integer, giving a path difference of nλ.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Resonance occurs when the frequency of an external periodic force equals the:
questions.explanation: Resonance occurs when the driving frequency matches the natural frequency, producing a large response when damping is sufficiently small.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to the law of reflection, the angle of reflection is:

options.text: Always twice the angle of incidence
Equal to the angle of incidence
Independent of the angle of incidence

questions.explanation: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, with both angles measured from the normal to the reflecting surface.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When light passes obliquely from air into glass, it generally bends:

options.text: Along the surface in every case
Backwards along its original path in every case

questions.explanation: Light entering glass from air slows down and, for oblique incidence, refracts towards the normal because glass has a higher refractive index.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Total internal reflection can occur when light travels:

options.text: From a rarer to a denser medium at any angle
From a denser to a rarer medium with incidence angle greater than the critical angle

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection requires light to travel from a higher-index medium to a lower-index medium, with incidence angle exceeding the critical angle.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the power of a converging lens with focal length +0.5 m?
questions.explanation: Lens power P = 1/f when focal length is in metres. Thus P = 1/0.5 = +2 dioptres.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the approximate magnitude of the elementary charge?
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the elementary charge is approximately 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ coulombs. A proton carries positive charge and an electron carries the negative of this value.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the separation between two point charges is doubled, what happens to the magnitude of the electrostatic force, assuming the charges remain unchanged?
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law gives force proportional to 1/r². Doubling the separation reduces the force to 1/4 of its original value.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Electric potential difference is defined as:
questions.explanation: Potential difference is the work done per unit charge in moving a test charge between two points, with the sign depending on the work convention used.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A capacitor stores a charge of 6 μC at a potential difference of 3 V. What is its capacitance?
questions.explanation: Capacitance C = Q/V = 6 μC / 3 V = 2 μF.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An appliance operates at 220 V and draws a current of 2 A. What is its electrical power?
questions.explanation: Electrical power P = VI = 220 × 2 = 440 W.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two resistors of 6 Ω each are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
questions.explanation: For two equal resistors R in parallel, the equivalent resistance is R/2. Thus, 6/2 = 3 Ω.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: One kilowatt-hour is equal to:
questions.explanation: One kilowatt-hour is 1000 W × 3600 s = 3.6 × 10⁶ joules.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charged particle moves parallel to a uniform magnetic field. What is the magnetic force on it?
questions.explanation: The magnetic force magnitude is |q|vB sin θ. For parallel motion, θ = 0°, so the force is zero.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.subtopic: Magnetic field around a current-carrying wire
questions.question: The magnetic field lines around a long straight current-carrying wire form:

options.text: Straight lines parallel to the wire
Concentric circles centred on the wire

questions.explanation: The magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying conductor forms concentric circles, with direction determined by the right-hand grip rule.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Faraday's law, the magnitude of induced EMF depends on the rate of change of:
questions.explanation: Faraday's law states that induced EMF is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage through a circuit.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the frequency of a photon doubles, what happens to its energy?
questions.explanation: Photon energy is E = hf. Since Planck's constant is fixed, doubling frequency doubles photon energy.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For light incident on a suitable metal, increasing the light intensity while keeping its frequency above the threshold generally increases the:

options.text: Maximum kinetic energy of each emitted electron
Number of emitted photoelectrons per unit time

questions.explanation: At fixed frequency above the threshold, greater intensity generally means more incident photons per unit time and therefore more emitted photoelectrons. Maximum kinetic energy depends on frequency.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is inversely proportional to its:
questions.explanation: The de Broglie relation is λ = h/p, where h is Planck's constant and p is the particle's momentum.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following particles has no electric charge?
questions.explanation: A neutron has zero net electric charge. Protons and positrons are positively charged, while electrons are negatively charged.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The moment of inertia of a rigid body about a specified axis depends on:

options.text: The distribution of its mass relative to the axis

questions.explanation: Moment of inertia is the sum or integral of mass elements multiplied by the square of their perpendicular distance from the rotation axis. It depends on mass distribution and the chosen axis.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The magnitude of torque produced by a force F acting at perpendicular distance r from an axis is:
questions.explanation: Torque magnitude equals force multiplied by the perpendicular moment arm: τ = Fr.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the net external torque on a system is zero, which quantity is conserved?

options.text: Moment of inertia in every case
Rotational kinetic energy in every case

questions.explanation: Zero net external torque means angular momentum remains constant. Rotational kinetic energy need not remain constant if the system's configuration changes.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a rigid body rolling without slipping on a stationary surface, the relationship between centre-of-mass speed v and angular speed ω is:
questions.explanation: The no-slip condition gives v = ωr, where r is the rolling body's radius.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In simple harmonic motion, acceleration is related to displacement x by:
questions.explanation: Simple harmonic motion has acceleration proportional to displacement and opposite in direction: a = −ω²x.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For small oscillations, what happens to the time period of a simple pendulum if its length is multiplied by four?
questions.explanation: The time period is T = 2π√(L/g). Multiplying L by four multiplies T by √4 = 2.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For steady flow of an ideal fluid along a streamline, where the fluid speed increases and height remains constant, the static pressure generally:
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's equation states that pressure plus kinetic energy per unit volume plus gravitational potential energy per unit volume is constant along a streamline for ideal steady flow. At constant height, greater speed corresponds to lower static pressure.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For steady incompressible flow through a pipe, the continuity equation is:
questions.explanation: For incompressible steady flow, volume flow rate is conserved, so cross-sectional area multiplied by flow speed remains constant.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Using the convention that W is work done by the system, the first law of thermodynamics is:
questions.explanation: With Q defined as heat added to the system and W as work done by the system, the first law is ΔU = Q − W.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The thermal efficiency of a heat engine is defined as:

options.text: Heat rejected divided by work output
Work output divided by heat absorbed
Heat absorbed divided by work output
Work output multiplied by heat absorbed

questions.explanation: Thermal efficiency is useful work output divided by heat absorbed from the hot reservoir: η = W/Qₕ.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electric field at a point is defined as the:

options.text: Force per unit positive test charge

questions.explanation: Electric field E is force per unit positive test charge: E = F/q for a sufficiently small test charge that does not disturb the field.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electric potential energy of a charge q at electric potential V, taking zero reference consistently, is:
questions.explanation: Electric potential is potential energy per unit charge, so U = qV.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The electric dipole moment vector points from:

options.text: The midpoint in an arbitrary direction
The electric field towards the charge centre in every case

questions.explanation: The electric dipole moment vector is conventionally directed from the negative charge to the positive charge.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Kirchhoff's current law at a circuit junction follows from conservation of:
questions.explanation: Kirchhoff's current law states that the total current entering a junction equals the total current leaving it, expressing conservation of charge.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Kirchhoff's voltage law states that the algebraic sum of potential differences around a closed circuit loop is:
questions.explanation: Kirchhoff's voltage law expresses energy conservation: the algebraic sum of voltage rises and drops around a closed loop is zero.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When a cell supplies current to an external circuit, its terminal voltage is generally:

options.text: Greater than its EMF by the internal voltage drop
Less than its EMF because of internal resistance
Independent of current and internal resistance

questions.explanation: For a discharging cell, terminal voltage V = E − Ir, where E is EMF, I is current, and r is internal resistance.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A straight wire of length L carries current I perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B. What is the magnetic force magnitude?
questions.explanation: The force on a straight current-carrying conductor is F = BIL sin θ. For a perpendicular wire, sin 90° = 1, so F = BIL.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Lenz's law determines the direction of induced current so that it:

options.text: Always reinforces the change in magnetic flux
Opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it
Does not produce a magnetic field

questions.explanation: Lenz's law states that the induced current's magnetic effect opposes the change in flux responsible for the induction, consistent with energy conservation.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a sinusoidal alternating voltage with peak value V₀, the RMS voltage is:
questions.explanation: For a sinusoidal waveform, the RMS voltage equals the peak voltage divided by √2.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An ideal transformer has 100 turns in its primary coil and 500 turns in its secondary coil. If the primary voltage is 20 V, what is the secondary voltage?
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, Vs/Vp = Ns/Np = 500/100 = 5. Therefore Vs = 5 × 20 = 100 V.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the highest frequency?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays occupy the highest-frequency, shortest-wavelength region of the electromagnetic spectrum among these choices.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In Young's double-slit experiment, fringe width is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Fringe width β = λD/d, where λ is wavelength, D is the slit-to-screen distance, and d is slit separation. Therefore, fringe width is proportional to wavelength.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Diffraction is most noticeable when the size of an opening is comparable to the:

options.text: Density of the surrounding medium only

questions.explanation: Diffraction becomes pronounced when the size of an aperture or obstacle is comparable to the wavelength of the wave.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Polarization demonstrates that light is:
questions.explanation: Polarization restricts the direction of transverse oscillations and is evidence that light is a transverse electromagnetic wave.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The work function of a metal is the minimum energy required to:

options.text: Remove an electron from the metal surface
Create a proton inside the nucleus
Double the mass of an electron

questions.explanation: The work function is the minimum energy needed to release an electron from a metal surface under the specified conditions.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The threshold frequency of a metal is related to its work function φ by:
questions.explanation: At the threshold frequency f₀, photon energy just equals the work function: φ = hf₀.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In the Bohr model of hydrogen, an electron emits a photon when it:

options.text: Moves from a lower energy level to a higher level
Moves from a higher energy level to a lower level
Remains permanently in the same energy level

questions.explanation: An electron emits a photon when it transitions from a higher energy state to a lower one. The photon energy equals the difference between the two levels.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The visible spectral lines of hydrogen belong primarily to which series?
questions.explanation: The Balmer series consists of transitions ending at n = 2 in hydrogen and includes prominent visible spectral lines.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The mass defect of a nucleus is associated with its:
questions.explanation: The mass defect corresponds to the difference between the sum of the constituent nucleon masses and the actual nuclear mass. Its energy equivalent is the nuclear binding energy.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Nuclear fission is the process in which:

options.text: Two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus
A heavy nucleus splits into lighter nuclei
An electron changes its orbital direction only
A chemical bond forms without nuclear change

questions.explanation: In nuclear fission, a heavy nucleus splits into smaller nuclei, often releasing energy and additional neutrons.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Nuclear fusion is the process in which:

options.text: Light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus
A heavy nucleus always splits spontaneously

questions.explanation: Fusion combines light nuclei into a heavier nucleus and can release energy when the products have greater binding energy per nucleon than the reactants.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: After three half-lives, what fraction of the original radioactive nuclei remains undecayed?
questions.explanation: The remaining fraction after n half-lives is (1/2)ⁿ. After three half-lives, it is (1/2)³ = 1/8.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Adding a suitable pentavalent impurity to pure silicon generally produces which type of semiconductor?
questions.explanation: Pentavalent donor impurities provide additional electrons, producing n-type silicon in which electrons are the majority charge carriers.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a typical p-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are:
questions.explanation: Trivalent acceptor doping creates holes as the majority carriers in p-type semiconductors, although electrons remain as minority carriers.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The main function of a rectifier circuit is to convert:
questions.explanation: A rectifier uses components such as diodes to convert alternating current into a unidirectional, usually pulsating DC output.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a transistor operating in the common-emitter configuration, the current gain β is defined as:

options.text: Collector current divided by base current
Base current divided by collector current
Emitter voltage divided by collector voltage
Collector resistance divided by base resistance

questions.explanation: The common-emitter current gain is β = I_C/I_B, where I_C is collector current and I_B is base current under the specified operating conditions.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In amplitude modulation, which property of the carrier wave varies according to the message signal?
questions.explanation: In amplitude modulation, the carrier amplitude varies with the message signal while the carrier frequency remains nominally fixed.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For conventional double-sideband amplitude modulation with a single-tone message of frequency fₘ, the required transmission bandwidth is:
questions.explanation: Conventional double-sideband AM produces sidebands at the carrier frequency plus and minus the message frequency, giving a total bandwidth of 2fₘ.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to mass-energy equivalence, the rest energy of a body of mass m is:
questions.explanation: Einstein's mass-energy relation gives rest energy E₀ = mc², where c is the speed of light in vacuum.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to special relativity, a moving clock measured by an inertial observer who sees it moving runs:

options.text: Faster than the observer's identical stationary clock in all frames
Slower than the observer's clock, when compared using the standard inertial-frame setup
At a rate independent of relative speed

questions.explanation: Time dilation means a moving clock is measured to tick more slowly relative to an inertial frame in which it is moving. Comparisons of separated clocks require care about the reference frame and synchronization.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The moment of inertia of a body depends on which of the following?

options.text: Distribution of mass about the axis
Position of the axis of rotation

questions.explanation: Moment of inertia depends on the mass distribution relative to the chosen axis and therefore changes when the axis changes. It does not depend directly on angular velocity.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A rotating body has moment of inertia I and angular velocity ω. Its angular momentum about the axis is:
questions.explanation: For rotation about a fixed principal axis, angular momentum is L = Iω.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A force of 10 N acts perpendicular to a lever arm of length 0.5 m. What is the torque about the pivot?
questions.explanation: Torque magnitude is τ = rF sin θ. Since the force is perpendicular, τ = 0.5 × 10 = 5 N m.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A skater spins faster by pulling their arms inward. Which quantities are conserved if external torque is negligible?

options.text: Rotational kinetic energy in every case

questions.explanation: With negligible external torque, angular momentum remains constant. Pulling the arms inward reduces moment of inertia and increases angular velocity.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the rotational kinetic energy of a body with moment of inertia 2 kg m² rotating at 3 rad/s?
questions.explanation: Rotational kinetic energy is K = ½Iω² = ½ × 2 × 3² = 9 J.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In simple harmonic motion, the acceleration is:

options.text: Directly proportional to displacement and in the same direction
Proportional to displacement and opposite in direction

questions.explanation: In SHM, acceleration satisfies a = −ω²x, so it is proportional to displacement but directed toward the equilibrium position.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For small oscillations, the time period of a simple pendulum depends on:
